text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty -> #incidents: High error rate from ap-southeast-2c (AZ-b) affecting inference endpoints serving customer traffic. Priority: P1. Escalation: on-call SRE.

 dave_oncall: I’m on it. Seeing alerts from our ELB health checks and increased 502s and TLS handshakes failing. Impacting ~15% of requests to hosted models in ap-southeast-2. Opening bridge now.

 maya_eng: Thanks — I can join bridge in 2 min. Quick status: our edge ELBs in ap-southeast-2b show ~30% unhealthy targets. Route53 health checks also flapping for the same subset.

 seung_net: Observed packet loss on ENIs in azb earlier. Net telem shows retransmits + high latency from azb->edge proxy. Could be a local AZ-network egress issue.

 ben_platform: Repro steps I ran: curl to a few affected ELB IPs shows TLS handshake timeouts or immediate 502s. Sample:```
$ curl -v https://elb-aps2-prod-123.us-east.example.com/health
* Connected to 10.23.45.67 (10.23.45.67) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed, but server returned HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```

 lucy_support: Customers already flagged errors on a major tenant (chat feature degraded). We’ve opened support tickets and told them we’re investigating. Need ETA for external comms.

 dave_oncall: Short-term mitigation plan: 1) Disable AZ-b as a weighted route in Route53 for public endpoints, shifting traffic to ap-southeast-2a/c and us-west-2 fallback. 2) Increase ELB healthcheck sensitivity and drain bad targets. 3) Open AWS support case for ENI/az connectivity.

 seung_net: If we remove AZ-b from weighted records, TTLs matter — current Route53 TTL is 60s for the weighted record, but some caches may hold. We can temporarily lower TTL to 10s before switching to speed convergence.

 maya_eng: I’ll prepare the change. Steps I’ll run:```
# lower TTL on service.example.com WRS record to 10
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch file://lower-ttl.json
# update weighted records to 0 weight for aps2-azb pool
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch file://zero-weight-azb.json
```

 ben_platform: One caveat: some internal traffic uses private routing to AZ-b (dedicated VPC peering). We need to ensure internal private endpoints also get drained or have a fallback. I can push a config to the proxy routing table to avoid azb targets.

 dave_oncall: Do it. Also increase connection timeout on edge proxy for retriable 502s to avoid immediate failures while draining.

 lucy_support: Outgoing comms plan: Draft a short message: “We’re investigating increased error rates in ap-southeast-2. We have shifted traffic and are working with cloud provider. We will update in 15 minutes.” I’ll post once we have confirmation of traffic shift.

 incident-bot: AWS Support case created: case# 9876543210 — Contact: SE escalations. Getting initial logs.

 seung_net: AWS console shows ENI metrics for the affected AZ with elevated TX errors and saturation on a subset of network devices. Filing a networking escalation.

 maya_eng: Executed TTL lower -> 10s and started change batch to zero weight for AZ-b. Started scaling up capacity in neighbouring AZs to absorb traffic (increase instance counts in aps2-a/c by +20%).

 ben_platform: Applied proxy routing change for private endpoints to avoid AZ-b pools. Also updated autoscaling policy to ensure warm capacity in other AZs.

 dave_oncall: Monitoring after change — Route53 queries for service.example.com show >90% now resolving to ips in az-a/c and us-west-2 fallback. ELB target health in azb still flapping but traffic shifted.

 maya_eng: Observability: error rate for customer-facing endpoints dropped from 18% -> 2% aggregate within 90s of change. Latency back to baseline for most tenants.

 lucy_support: Notifying customers: posting update now with mitigation steps and ETA for full resolution (we’ll keep AZ-b disabled until AWS confirms network stability).

 aws-support: AWS: We’re seeing a partial networking disruption affecting ENI egress within ap-southeast-2b. Our NOC is investigating a fabric-level issue. We recommend keeping traffic shifted while we remediate.

 seung_net: AWS recommends a full instance-level rebind for a subset of affected hosts (detach/reattach ENI). That’s disruptive — prefer we wait for AWS NOC guidance.

 ben_platform: For the internal private routes where rebind isn’t an option, we implemented temporary flow-steering at the proxy layer to skip problematic hosts. That seems stable so far.

 dave_oncall: Next steps: 1) Keep AZ-b weight=0 in Route53 2) Keep autoscaling adjustments for 30m and monitor error budgets 3) Coordinate with AWS for ENI remediation and get confirmation before reintroducing AZ-b 4) Post an incident summary after bridge.

 maya_eng: I’ll schedule a canary reintroduce once AWS confirms. Add a regression eval to Redwood Optimize to watch for latent token-level errors after reintroduction.

 lucy_support: Support notes: Logged impacted tenants, estimated 15% of customer traffic hit, primary symptom 502s/TLS handshake fails. No data loss. Customers asked for postmortem and ETA for reenable.

 dave_oncall: Thanks everyone. Bridge stood down for active coordination — monitoring only. If AWS resolves, we’ll test reintroduce with 1% weight then ramp.

 incident-bot: Post-incident checklist created and assigned: incident-doc task for SRE lead, comms draft for success team, follow-up with AWS case.

 seung_net: AWS updated: fabric NOC has rolled a fix to routing plane in aps2. They report improvement; metrics trending down. Recommend wait 10 minutes then health-check targets.

 maya_eng: Rolling a controlled test: set AZ-b weight to 1% and watch.

 ben_platform: Canary shows 1% -> no immediate 502 spike, latency ok. Gradually ramping to 10% over 5m.

 lucy_support: Telling customers we’re reintroducing AZ-b in canary mode. Will update if anything changes.

 dave_oncall: Ramp to 50% of previous baseline over 10m, keep Route53 weights symmetric. Observability: still nominal.

 seung_net: Final confirmation from AWS: fabric fix validated by us and provider. They’ll keep monitoring.

 dave_oncall: Restoring original weights. Setting TTL back to 60s after propagation stabilized.

 lucy_support: Final customer update sent: "Issue in ap-southeast-2 (AZ-b) caused elevated errors. We shifted traffic, worked with cloud provider, and reintroduced capacity gradually. Service is restored; we’re doing a post-incident analysis and follow-up."

 maya_eng: Postmortem owner assigned. Key action items: add more aggressive cross-AZ traffic steering on partial network failures, add automated Route53 weighted failover runbook, and include ENI saturation alarms in SLO dashboards.

 dave_oncall: Closing bridge. Thanks team — great coordination. :tada:
